title: Sultan of Yogyakarta
capsule: The Sultanate of Yogyakarta was established on 13 February 1755 under the Treaty of Giyanti, which split the weakened Mataram Sultanate and granted the western half to Sri Sultan Hamengkubuwono I (r. 1755–1792), a capable military commander who had fought against both VOC intervention and rival claimants. Hamengkubuwono I consolidated his realm and built the Kraton of Yogyakarta, making the sultanate the dominant cultural centre of Javanese court tradition. His son Hamengkubuwono II had three interrupted reigns due to repeated Dutch deposition, and the sultanate's sovereignty was formally curtailed by the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1830 following the Java War (1825–1830) against the Dutch, in which Prince Diponegoro led Javanese resistance. The polity survived as a nominally autonomous principality under Dutch paramountcy until Indonesian independence in 1945.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The sultanate's boundaries and political history from 1755 are documented in Dutch colonial records and local court chronicles (babad); territorial extent is reasonably well attested for the post-1755 period, though earlier Mataram-period boundary shifts complicate mapping.
